03Certificate

A certificate you can verify and share

After meeting the published course-completion criteria, learners can claim a certificate with its own credential ID and a public verification page. The certificate can be shared or saved as a PDF.

To earn it

  1. Finish every lesson
  2. Complete every lab step and pass its health checks
  3. Answer at least 70% of the check questions correctly, on the first try or in review

What you get

  • A credential ID and a public page that confirms it
  • Add to LinkedIn in one click
  • Share on LinkedIn, X or Facebook, or copy the link
  • Save as a PDF

The certificate records completion against the course rules, based on progress reported by the learner’s browser. It is self-reported and unproctored; lab work is not independently marked by Intellica. It is not accredited as a professional qualification and does not confer or replace an external certification.

04How we teach

Every course follows the same loop

Study expert practice

The Architecture and Cyber Security Academies connect core concepts to worked examples and decisions drawn from real engineering and security work.

Build professional artefacts

Guided labs turn learning into architecture descriptions, security designs, test plans and other work products that can be reviewed and improved.

Retrieve, test and improve

Knowledge checks, practical tools, model solutions and rubrics help learners identify gaps and improve the quality of their work.

Learn from current evidence

The academies cite research and standards, record review dates and update their materials as evidence and technology change.

Research behind the method

  • Test-enhanced learningRoediger & Karpicke, Psychological Science (2006)

    Low-stakes recall questions help strengthen delayed retention; they are used to retrieve knowledge, not merely score it.

    Read the research
  • Distributed and interleaved practiceCepeda et al. (2006); Kirschner et al., Educational Psychology Review (2026)

    Spacing and interleaving support durable learning when practice and feedback elicit the right cognitive work. The 2026 meta-analysis covers school classrooms; its effect sizes should not be assumed for adult professional training.

    Read the research
  • Worked examples and scaffold fadingRenkl, Cognitive Science (2014 issue; first published 2013)

    Learners first inspect a complete worked solution, then complete partially supported tasks before independent performance.

    Read the research
  • Active learningFreeman et al., PNAS (2014)

    Applied tasks, explanation and decision-making supplement exposition; passive reading is not treated as evidence of competence.

    Read the research
  • Feedback and deliberate practiceHattie & Timperley (2007); Ericsson et al. (1993)

    Rubrics and model solutions make gaps visible; repeated practice is targeted at a specific weakness and followed by corrective feedback.

    Read the research
  • Deliberate practiceEricsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer, Psychological Review (1993)

    Practice is targeted at a defined performance gap, repeated with informative feedback and adjusted as competence improves; seat time alone is not a measure of expertise.

    Read the research

Every course page identifies its current delivery status, the work it asks you to complete, how completion is recorded and how it relates to external qualifications. Available courses are distinguished from planned levels and assessments.
